title: Domain interpretation fork vs shared reflection authority

scope.idea: RINSE should have one evidence-bound interpretation semantics; domain modules may project it but must not create competing interpretation authority.

past.summary: Reflection Graph v0.2 was developed in the stacked #21 -> #20 -> #23 branch chain while main still exposed the older core.

present.summary: Career RINSE #24 was developed separately from main and introduced its own provisional interpretation object with independent IDs/confidence fields, while the reflection graph defined versioned records, evidence relations, missing evidence and authority semantics.

future.summary: The reflection graph is the sole semantic authority; Career consumes it as a domain adapter and exposes convenience projections bound to reflection_record_id.

evidence.claim: Reflection Graph v0.2 defines versioned record identity, evidence/status compatibility, temporal fields, missing evidence and REFLECTION_ONLY non-executable authority.
Career v0.1 independently derived provisional interpretation objects with separate IDs and confidence semantics.
The #21 -> #20 -> #23 chain is now consolidated into one promotion surface directly against main.
Career v0.2 creates shared reflection records first and derives its career-friendly interpretation view from those exact record IDs.
Tests bind Career projections to reflection_record_id and preserve core SUPPORTED/SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS/CONTESTED/INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE plus non-executable authority semantics.

causalPath.statement: The new core interpretation contract remained in a stacked branch chain rather than becoming the single active base for later domain work.
Career RINSE evolved from main and necessarily invented a separate interpretation shape because the reflection contract was not its parent surface.
Two active definitions of a RINSE interpretation can diverge in identity, evidence, status, time and authority semantics.
Consolidate the core promotion surface and make Career produce reflection_record.v0.2 records before generating any domain projection.

navigation.reason: The duplicate domain semantics are explained by repository promotion topology rather than by one incorrect Career rule.

refactor.change: Use one reflection-record authority; retain Career-only normalization, evidence classification, redaction, portfolio and contact projections; bind career interpretation views to reflection_record_id.
refactor.expectedEffect: New RINSE domains can add adapters and views without multiplying interpretation contracts or authority semantics.
